title: Add up four cubes
hook: 1, 8, 27, 64: the cubes grow fast. Does their total make any shape at all?

knows: that k³ means k × k × k
doesNotKnow: that 1³ + 2³ + … + n³ is a perfect square, the square of 1 + 2 + … + n

misconception: Sums of cubes have no pattern; or the total is about the size of the last cube.
objective: The learner can lay 1, 2, 3 and 4 squares of side 1, 2, 3 and 4 into one 10 × 10 square and say that 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + 4³ = (1 + 2 + 3 + 4)² = 100.

claims.text: k³ = k × k × k is k squares of k × k laid flat; for example 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 is two squares of 2 × 2.
1 + 8 + 27 + 64 = 100 cells fill a 10 × 10 square with nothing left over; after each cube the side is 1, 3, 6, 10.
claims.source: Demo.tsx layer(k) lays k squares of side k as an L-band from side T(k−1) to T(k); a node check (artifacts not committed) confirmed each band has area k³ and the four bands cover all 100 cells exactly once. T(k)² − T(k−1)² = k³.

claims.text: 64 is only the last cube, and 30 is 1² + 2² + 3² + 4².
The pattern holds for every n (it can be proved by induction); this picture shows n = 4.
claims.source: Nicomachus's theorem: Σ k³ = (n(n + 1)/2)²; induction step (T(n+1))² − T(n)² = (n + 1)³. The tiling is shown for n = 4 only (brief 47 claim 3).

recall.question: 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + 4³ + 5³ is the square of which number?
recall.why: The sum of the first n cubes is (1 + 2 + … + n)². 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15, so the total is 225.
